blurb: The check reads the PATH assignments in the global initialization files, the login and non-login shell startup files along with the environment and security files. A finding is any PATH entry that is relative, meaning it does not begin with a slash, or empty, meaning a leading, trailing, or doubled colon. A relative or empty entry lets a shell resolve a command from the current directory or another attacker-writable directory ahead of trusted system directories, so a malicious binary placed there runs with the privileges of the user who invokes the command.
